Connection/transaction context for netlink/rtnetlink operations. Holds the socket fd, local/peer addresses, and sequencing/dump state used while sending requests and receiving replies from the kernel.

objects.definition:
typedef int (*rtnl_filter_t)(const struct sockaddr_nl *,
			     struct nlmsghdr *n, void *);
objects.description: Callback function type used by rtnl_dump_filter, rtnl_listen, and similar APIs to process each received netlink message. Returns int status; arguments provide sender address, the message header, and user argument.
Small helper struct bundling a filter callback and its user argument for use with rtnl_dump_filter_l.

Process record used by Firejail to track processes. Includes flags (level, zombie), identifiers (parent pid, uid), and a union of optional per-process data: event info (user, cmd), CPU usage (utime, stime), or network stats (rx, tx). The union means only one of event/top/netstats is valid at a time. Storage is typically managed in a global array or buffer referenced by pids. Exact lifecycle and initialization rules are not documented in this header; consumers should zero-initialize before use and only access the active union member established by the producing code.

Pointer to the first element of a constant, null-terminated array of constant C strings that represent default library search paths. The array itself and the strings it points to are immutable. Defined elsewhere; only declared here.

Referenced in macros via offsetof to access fields arch, nr, and args[n], but the struct is not defined in this header. It is defined externally (in linux/seccomp.h). Since it is only referenced and not defined here, it should be ignored per the instructions.

objects.definition: typedef void (filter_fn)(int fd, int syscall, int arg, void *ptrarg, bool native);

Implementations receive the BPF/seccomp filter descriptor (fd), the syscall number (syscall), an auxiliary integer argument (arg), an optional pointer argument (ptrarg), and a flag indicating native architecture handling (native). Used by syscall_check_list to apply filtering actions per syscall entry.

functions.name: timetrace_start
functions.description: Marks the start of a time measurement interval for subsequent retrieval with timetrace_end. Intended for lightweight timing around a code region. Internal state is recorded on call; no arguments are required. Implementation details and scope/thread-safety are unknown.
requirements: Must be called before a corresponding call to timetrace_end to obtain a meaningful duration.
May not be thread-safe; avoid concurrent use from multiple threads unless documented otherwise (unknown).

functions.name: timetrace_end
functions.description: Ends a previously started timing interval and returns the elapsed time in seconds as a float. Complements timetrace_start. Exact timing source and precision are unknown.
requirements: timetrace_start must have been called earlier in the same context before calling timetrace_end.
The return value is a floating-point duration in seconds; callers should handle typical floating-point precision limits.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unknown; avoid concurrent use without external synchronization.

functions.name: join_namespace_by_fd
functions.description: Joins a Linux namespace identified by type using a directory file descriptor, likely referring to a /proc/<pid>/ns directory and the specified namespace entry (e.g., "net", "mnt"). Internally expected to use setns/openat to attach the current thread to the target namespace. Returns status as an int (conventionally 0 on success, non-zero on failure), but exact semantics are unknown.
requirements: dirfd must be a valid open file descriptor to a directory that contains namespace entries (commonly /proc/<pid>/ns).
typestr must be a valid NUL-terminated string naming a namespace (e.g., "net", "mnt", "ipc", "uts", "pid", "user", "cgroup").
Caller must have sufficient privileges/capabilities to join the target namespace (typically requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN or setns permission).
Calling this function changes the calling thread’s namespace; do not call if this side effect is undesirable.
Behavior on error (errno setting, return codes) is unknown; caller should treat non-zero return as failure.

functions.name: join_namespace
functions.description: Joins the specified namespace of a target process identified by pid. The namespace type is indicated by typestr (e.g., "net", "mnt"). Likely implemented via opening /proc/<pid>/ns/<typestr> and calling setns. Returns an int status (conventionally 0 on success, non-zero on failure), but specifics are unknown.
requirements: pid must refer to a running process whose namespace can be opened.
typestr must be a valid NUL-terminated string naming a Linux namespace (e.g., "net", "mnt", "ipc", "uts", "pid", "user", "cgroup").
Caller must have sufficient privileges/capabilities to join the target namespace.
Side effect: changes the calling thread’s namespace; ensure this is intended.
Behavior on error (return codes, errno) is unknown; treat non-zero return as failure.

functions.name: name2pid
functions.description: Resolves a process name to a process ID, storing the result in *pid. The matching strategy (exact, first found, or multiple matches) is unknown. Returns an int status (likely 0 on success) but exact semantics are unknown.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string representing a process name.
pid must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the resulting process ID.
If multiple processes match the name, the selection policy is unknown; callers should not assume which PID is returned.
Return code semantics are unknown; caller should check for non-zero as failure.

functions.name: pid_proc_comm
functions.description: Retrieves the comm (short command name) for the given process from /proc/<pid>/comm and returns it as a string. The allocation/ownership of the returned string is not documented and is unknown; expect NULL on failure.
requirements: pid must refer to an existing process accessible via /proc.
Caller must not assume the returned pointer’s lifetime or ownership model; freeing requirements are unknown.
Returned pointer may be NULL on error; caller must check for NULL before use.
The returned string is expected to be NUL-terminated; exact contents and trailing newline handling are unknown.

functions.name: pid_proc_cmdline
functions.description: Retrieves the full command line for the given process from /proc/<pid>/cmdline and returns it as a string. The formatting (spaces vs. NUL separators) and allocation/ownership are not documented and are unknown; expect NULL on failure.
requirements: pid must refer to an existing process accessible via /proc.
Caller must check for NULL return indicating failure.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned pointer is unknown; do not assume whether it must be freed.
Exact formatting of the cmdline string is unknown; caller should not rely on delimiter specifics.

functions.name: pid_proc_cmdline_x11_xpra_xephyr
functions.description: Examines the command line of the given process and returns an indicator related to X11/xpra/Xephyr usage (e.g., detection of these components). Exact return codes and criteria are unknown.
requirements: pid must refer to an existing, accessible process.
Return value semantics are unspecified; callers should treat non-zero/zero conventions as unknown and handle accordingly.
May read /proc/<pid>/cmdline; ensure sufficient permissions.

functions.name: pid_hidepid
functions.description: Checks system configuration related to hidepid on procfs (i.e., whether process details are hidden). Likely returns an int indicating the hidepid level or a boolean-like status, but exact semantics are unknown.
requirements: No arguments required.
Return value meaning is unspecified; caller should not assume specific levels without checking implementation.

functions.name: do_replace_cntrl_chars
functions.description: Replaces control characters in the provided string in place with the specified replacement character c. Returns the input pointer for convenience. The exact definition of control characters follows the implementation (likely iscntrl).
requirements: str must be a non-NULL, writable, NUL-terminated buffer.
Replacement character c should be a valid char; behavior for non-printable replacements is permitted but may be undesirable.
Caller must ensure sufficient buffer capacity is not required since replacement is in-place (no growth).
Function may return NULL on error (unknown); caller should check the return value before use.

functions.name: replace_cntrl_chars
functions.description: Returns a new string based on str with all control characters replaced by the given character c. Does not modify the input. Allocation details and ownership of the returned string are not documented and unknown; NULL may be returned on failure.
requirements: str must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string.
Caller must check for NULL return and handle allocation failures.
Caller should assume the returned string, if non-NULL, may need to be freed, but ownership is not documented (unknown).

functions.name: escape_cntrl_chars
functions.description: Produces an escaped representation of control characters in str (e.g., using backslash escapes), returning a new string. Exact escaping rules and allocation/ownership are not documented and unknown; NULL may be returned on failure.
requirements: str must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string.
Caller must check for NULL return before use.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned string is unspecified; freeing requirements are unknown.

functions.name: has_cntrl_chars
functions.description: Checks whether the input string contains any control characters. Returns an int indicating presence/absence; exact return convention (e.g., 0/1) is not documented but typically non-zero indicates presence.
requirements: str must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string.
Caller should not rely on the specific numeric return beyond boolean-like interpretation unless implementation is known.

functions.name: reject_cntrl_chars
functions.description: Validates that fname contains no control characters. On detecting invalid input, it likely reports an error and may terminate the program or throw an error, but exact behavior is unknown. Returns no value.
requirements: fname must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string.
Caller should be prepared for this function to abort the process or otherwise not return on validation failure (behavior unknown).
Use only with trusted strings or sanitize before calling to avoid unexpected termination.

functions.name: reject_meta_chars
functions.description: Validates that fname contains no shell meta-characters. If globbing is non-zero, some characters used for globbing (e.g., * and ?) might be allowed; exact policy is unknown. On violation, it likely reports an error and may terminate, but behavior is not documented.
requirements: fname must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string.
globbing is an integer flag; semantics are unknown beyond indicating whether globbing characters may be allowed.
Caller should be prepared for process termination or non-return on validation failure (behavior unknown).

functions.name: warn_dumpable
functions.description: Issues a warning if the current process is dumpable (i.e., core dumps and ptrace exposure). No return value. Intended for diagnostic/logging purposes. Exact warning mechanism is unknown.
requirements: No arguments required.
Caller should not expect a return value or a way to suppress output besides external configuration (unknown).

functions.name: gnu_basename
functions.description: Returns the final component of a filesystem path (GNU basename-like behavior) without modifying the input. The returned pointer may point into the input string or to an internal/static buffer; exact ownership and lifetime are unknown.
requirements: path must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string.
If the returned pointer aliases the input buffer, the input must remain valid for as long as the result is used.
Behavior for paths with trailing slashes or empty strings is unspecified.

functions.name: str_to_int_array
functions.description: Parses a string into an array of integers and returns a pointer to the array, storing the element count in *sz. The expected format (e.g., comma- or space-separated) is not documented and unknown. Returns NULL on failure (assumed).
requirements: str must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string containing a list of integers in the expected format (unknown).
sz must be a non-NULL pointer where the number of parsed elements will be written.
Caller must check for NULL return before use.
Allocation and ownership of the returned array are assumed to belong to the caller, requiring a corresponding free, but this is not documented (unknown).

functions.name: firejail_user_check
functions.description: Checks whether the specified user exists in the internal Firejail user database. Returns 1 if the user is found or if the database was not created. Usage: call to test for a user’s presence in the database; note that a return value of 1 also occurs when the database does not exist, so callers cannot distinguish between “found” and “no database” based on the return value alone. Other return values and error signaling are not documented in this header and are unknown.
requirements: name must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a NUL-terminated C string representing a username (inferred from signature).
Callers must not assume what non-1 return values mean; only the condition “1 means user found or database not created” is documented.
Behavior for empty strings, non-existent users, or invalid characters is not documented; callers should avoid clearly invalid inputs unless testing error paths (inferred).
Thread-safety, reentrancy, and side effects are not documented and are unknown.

functions.name: firejail_user_add
functions.description: Adds the specified user to the internal Firejail user database. Usage: call to record a user into the database; exact behavior on duplicates, database creation, persistence, and error handling is not documented in this header and remains unknown.
requirements: name must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a NUL-terminated C string representing a username (inferred from signature).
The function does not report errors via its return type; callers cannot detect failures from the signature alone.
Behavior if the database does not exist, if the user already exists, or if the name is empty/invalid is not documented and is unknown.
Required privileges, side effects, thread-safety, and persistence guarantees are not documented and are unknown.

functions.name: rtnl_open
functions.description: Opens and initializes a NETLINK_ROUTE socket and binds it to the requested multicast group subscriptions, storing state in rth. Typical usage is to prepare rth, call rtnl_open with desired groups, use the handle for send/receive, then call rtnl_close.
requirements: rth must be a valid, writable pointer to an uninitialized or reusable rtnl_handle structure.
Must be paired with rtnl_close to release resources.
subscriptions is a bitmask of netlink multicast groups for NETLINK_ROUTE; 0 is allowed for no groups.
Function must be called before using rth with other rtnl_* operations.

functions.name: rtnl_open_byproto
functions.signature: int rtnl_open_byproto(struct rtnl_handle *rth, unsigned subscriptions, int protocol)
functions.description: Opens and initializes a netlink socket using the specified protocol (e.g., NETLINK_ROUTE) and binds it to the given subscriptions. Stores socket and sequence state in rth.
requirements: rth must be a valid, writable pointer to rtnl_handle.
protocol must be a valid netlink protocol number (e.g., NETLINK_ROUTE).
Must be followed by rtnl_close to clean up.
Must be called before using rth for send/receive operations.
subscriptions is a bitmask of groups for the given protocol; may be 0.

functions.name: rtnl_close
functions.description: Closes the netlink socket and clears resources associated with the rtnl_handle.
requirements: rth must point to a previously opened rtnl_handle (via rtnl_open/rtnl_open_byproto).
It is safe only after all pending operations with rth have completed.
Do not use rth for further I/O after calling this function.

functions.name: rtnl_wilddump_request
functions.signature: int rtnl_wilddump_request(struct rtnl_handle *rth, int fam, int type)
functions.description: Sends a generic (wild) dump request over netlink for the specified address family and message type, initiating a dump sequence to fetch multiple objects (e.g., links, addresses, routes).
requirements: rth must be an open rtnl_handle.
fam is an AF_* address family (e.g., AF_UNSPEC, AF_INET).
type must be a valid RTM_* message type corresponding to a dump/get operation.
Caller should be prepared to receive a multipart netlink dump until NLMSG_DONE or an error is received.

functions.name: rtnl_wilddump_req_filter
functions.signature: int rtnl_wilddump_req_filter(struct rtnl_handle *rth, int fam, int type, __u32 filt_mask)
functions.description: Sends a dump request like rtnl_wilddump_request but includes an implementation-defined filter mask to reduce results.
requirements: rth must be an open rtnl_handle.
fam is an AF_* address family.
type is a valid RTM_* message type for dump/get.
filt_mask is a 32-bit filter bitmask; semantics depend on the requested object type.
Caller should be prepared to receive multipart dump replies.

functions.name: rtnl_dump_request
functions.signature: int rtnl_dump_request(struct rtnl_handle *rth, int type, void *req, int len)
functions.description: Sends a netlink dump request message of the given type with the provided request payload of length len on the handle rth.
requirements: rth must be an open rtnl_handle.
type must be a valid RTM_* (or protocol-specific) request message type.
If req is non-NULL, it must point to at least len bytes; len must be non-negative.
The formed message must not exceed socket send buffer limits; caller should ensure req/len are appropriate for kernel expectations.

functions.name: rtnl_dump_filter_l
functions.signature: int rtnl_dump_filter_l(struct rtnl_handle *rth, const struct rtnl_dump_filter_arg *arg)
functions.description: Receives and iterates over a multipart dump reply on rth, invoking the provided filter callback and passing through the user argument stored in arg. Low-level variant using a struct argument.
requirements: rth must be an open rtnl_handle, typically after issuing a dump request.
arg must be non-NULL and arg->filter must be a valid function pointer of type rtnl_filter_t.
The callback must handle netlink messages until completion; it should return appropriate codes as expected by the library (implementation-defined).

functions.name: rtnl_dump_filter
functions.signature: int rtnl_dump_filter(struct rtnl_handle *rth, rtnl_filter_t filter, void *arg)
functions.description: Receives and iterates over a multipart dump on rth, invoking the provided filter callback for each message, passing arg to the callback. Convenience wrapper around rtnl_dump_filter_l.
requirements: rth must be an open rtnl_handle, typically after issuing a dump request.
filter must be a valid function pointer of type rtnl_filter_t.
The callback must be prepared to handle NLMSG_ERROR, NLMSG_DONE, and data messages as delivered by the kernel.

functions.name: rtnl_talk
functions.signature: int rtnl_talk(struct rtnl_handle *rtnl, struct nlmsghdr *n, pid_t peer, unsigned groups, struct nlmsghdr *answer)
functions.description: Sends a netlink request message n over handle rtnl to the specified peer or groups and waits for a single reply or error. On success, optionally returns the reply in answer.
requirements: rtnl must be an open rtnl_handle.
n must point to a fully formed netlink message (proper nlmsg_len and headers).
peer is the destination PID (0 for kernel) when unicasting; groups is a multicast groups bitmask when applicable.
If answer is non-NULL, it must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the expected reply message; exact size requirements are implementation-defined.
Caller must check the return value for errors from the kernel (e.g., via NLMSG_ERROR).

functions.name: rtnl_send
functions.signature: int rtnl_send(struct rtnl_handle *rth, const void *buf, int len)
functions.description: Sends a raw buffer containing one or more netlink messages over the handle rth.
requirements: rth must be an open rtnl_handle.
buf must point to at least len bytes of data representing valid netlink message(s).
len must be non-negative and should respect socket send buffer limits.
Caller should check the return value to ensure the entire buffer was sent.

functions.name: rtnl_send_check
functions.signature: int rtnl_send_check(struct rtnl_handle *rth, const void *buf, int len)
functions.description: Sends a netlink request buffer and performs an immediate check for an acknowledgment or error from the kernel.
requirements: rth must be an open rtnl_handle.
buf must point to at least len bytes; len must be non-negative.
Caller must handle negative return values to detect kernel-side errors (via NLMSG_ERROR ACK).

functions.name: addattr
functions.signature: int addattr(struct nlmsghdr *n, int maxlen, int type)
functions.description: Appends an empty netlink attribute of the given type to the message n, adjusting lengths and alignment. Used for flags or presence-only attributes.
requirements: n must point to a writable, properly initialized nlmsghdr with sufficient space up to maxlen.
maxlen must be the total size of the output buffer holding n; it must be large enough for the new attribute including header and alignment.
type must be a valid attribute type for the target message.

functions.name: addattr8
functions.signature: int addattr8(struct nlmsghdr *n, int maxlen, int type, __u8 data)
functions.description: Appends an attribute of the given type with an 8-bit payload to the message n.
requirements: n must point to a writable, properly initialized nlmsghdr within a buffer of size maxlen.
There must be enough tailroom in the buffer for the attribute header and 1 byte payload with alignment.
type must be valid for the message context.

functions.name: addattr16
functions.signature: int addattr16(struct nlmsghdr *n, int maxlen, int type, __u16 data)
functions.description: Appends an attribute of the given type with a 16-bit payload to the message n.
requirements: n must be a writable message within a buffer of size maxlen.
Buffer must have space for the attribute header and 2-byte payload with alignment.
type must be valid for the message context.

functions.name: addattr32
functions.signature: int addattr32(struct nlmsghdr *n, int maxlen, int type, __u32 data)
functions.description: Appends an attribute of the given type with a 32-bit payload to the message n.
requirements: n must be writable and initialized; maxlen is the total buffer size.
Sufficient space must exist for header + 4-byte payload + alignment.
type must be valid for the message context.

functions.name: addattr64
functions.signature: int addattr64(struct nlmsghdr *n, int maxlen, int type, __u64 data)
functions.description: Appends an attribute of the given type with a 64-bit payload to the message n.
requirements: n must be writable and initialized; maxlen is the total buffer size.
Sufficient space must exist for header + 8-byte payload + alignment.
type must be valid for the message context.

functions.name: addattrstrz
functions.signature: int addattrstrz(struct nlmsghdr *n, int maxlen, int type, const char *data)
functions.description: Appends a string attribute of the given type to the message n, including the terminating NUL byte (strz).
requirements: n must be writable and initialized within a buffer of size maxlen.
data must be a valid NUL-terminated C string; its length including NUL must fit in the remaining buffer space with alignment.
type must be valid for the message context.

functions.name: addattr_l
functions.signature: int addattr_l(struct nlmsghdr *n, int maxlen, int type, const void *data, int alen)
functions.description: Appends an attribute of the given type with an arbitrary payload of length alen to the message n.
requirements: n must be writable and initialized within a buffer of size maxlen.
If alen > 0, data must point to at least alen bytes; alen must be non-negative.
Buffer must have enough space for header + alen bytes + alignment.
type must be valid for the message context.

functions.name: addraw_l
functions.signature: int addraw_l(struct nlmsghdr *n, int maxlen, const void *data, int len)
functions.description: Appends raw bytes directly to the end of the netlink message n without adding an attribute header. Used for embedding nested structures or message bodies.
requirements: n must be writable within a buffer of size maxlen.
If len > 0, data must point to at least len bytes; len must be non-negative.
Caller is responsible for correctness and alignment of the appended raw data.

functions.name: addattr_nest
functions.signature: struct rtattr *addattr_nest(struct nlmsghdr *n, int maxlen, int type)
functions.description: Starts a nested attribute of the given type in message n and returns a pointer to the created rtattr header. Subsequent attributes should be added, then closed with addattr_nest_end.
requirements: n must be writable and initialized within a buffer of size maxlen.
Buffer must have sufficient remaining space for at least an empty attribute header.
The returned rtattr pointer must later be passed to addattr_nest_end to finalize the nested attribute.

functions.name: addattr_nest_end
functions.description: Finalizes a nested attribute previously created by addattr_nest by fixing up its length and alignment.
requirements: n must be the same message used to create nest and must still be writable.
nest must be a pointer previously returned by addattr_nest and still valid.
There must be no further modifications inside the nested attribute after calling this function.

functions.name: addattr_nest_compat
functions.signature: struct rtattr *addattr_nest_compat(struct nlmsghdr *n, int maxlen, int type, const void *data, int len)
functions.description: Starts a nested attribute with a compatibility header/payload for older kernels, initializing it with data of length len. Returns the rtattr pointer for later closure.
requirements: n must be writable within a buffer of size maxlen.
If len > 0, data must point to at least len bytes; len must be non-negative.
The returned rtattr must be finalized with addattr_nest_compat_end.

functions.name: addattr_nest_compat_end
functions.description: Finalizes a compatibility nested attribute started by addattr_nest_compat, fixing up its length and alignment.
requirements: n must be the same message used to create nest and must still be writable.
nest must be a pointer returned by addattr_nest_compat and still valid.

functions.name: rta_addattr32
functions.signature: int rta_addattr32(struct rtattr *rta, int maxlen, int type, __u32 data)
functions.description: Appends a 32-bit attribute of the given type to the nested attribute rta, adjusting rta->rta_len accordingly.
requirements: rta must point to a writable rtattr container with space for growth up to maxlen bytes.
maxlen is the total size of the enclosing buffer for rta; it must be large enough for header + 4-byte payload + alignment.
type must be valid for the nested context.

functions.name: rta_addattr_l
functions.signature: int rta_addattr_l(struct rtattr *rta, int maxlen, int type, const void *data, int alen)
functions.description: Appends an attribute with arbitrary payload length alen to the nested attribute rta.
requirements: rta must be writable and refer to a buffer whose total size is maxlen.
If alen > 0, data must point to at least alen bytes; alen must be non-negative.
There must be enough remaining capacity for header + alen + alignment.
type must be valid for the nested context.

functions.name: parse_rtattr
functions.signature: int parse_rtattr(struct rtattr *tb[], int max, struct rtattr *rta, int len)
functions.description: Parses a linear buffer of netlink attributes starting at rta with total length len into an array tb of pointers indexed by attribute type up to max. Unrecognized or out-of-range types are ignored.
requirements: tb must point to an array of at least max pointers; the function will write entries into tb indices 0..max.
rta may be NULL if len is 0; len must be non-negative and should not exceed the actual buffer size.
Attributes in the buffer must be well-formed (proper lengths and alignment) to avoid parse errors.

functions.name: __gcov_flush
functions.description: Flushes GCC/gcov coverage data: forces a write-out of current counters and then resets them. In this header, when built with GCC >= 11.1 and HAVE_GCOV defined, it is provided as a static function that calls __gcov_dump() followed by __gcov_reset(); on older GCC versions it is expected to be provided by the gcov runtime; when HAVE_GCOV is not defined it is a no-op macro. Typical usage is to call this to persist intermediate coverage to disk (e.g., .gcda files) and clear counters for the next measurement interval.
requirements: No arguments; may be called with no preconditions.

For actual coverage effects, the program must be compiled with GCC coverage instrumentation (e.g., -fprofile-arcs/-ftest-coverage or -fprofile-generate) and built with HAVE_GCOV defined so the real gcov symbols are available; otherwise this resolves to a no-op macro.

Behavior and availability are conditional on compiler/version macros: on GCC >= 11.1 it is defined here as a static function; on older GCC it is provided by the runtime; without HAVE_GCOV it does nothing.

functions.name: __gcov_dump
functions.description: Writes out current GCC/gcov coverage counters to persistent storage (typically .gcda files) without terminating the process. When HAVE_GCOV is not defined in this build, this name is a no-op macro in this header.
requirements: No arguments; may be called with no preconditions.
For any effect beyond a no-op, the program must be compiled with GCC coverage instrumentation and built with HAVE_GCOV defined so the gcov runtime is linked.

functions.name: __gcov_reset
functions.description: Resets in-memory GCC/gcov coverage counters to zero. Often used after __gcov_dump() to start a fresh coverage interval. When HAVE_GCOV is not defined in this build, this name is a no-op macro in this header.
requirements: No arguments; may be called with no preconditions.
For any effect beyond a no-op, the program must be compiled with GCC coverage instrumentation and built with HAVE_GCOV defined so the gcov runtime is linked.
